aftercare.title: Aftercare for a beach town
leads: Keep it clean, keep it out of the Pacific, the pool, and the sun until it is healed.
Salt water, chlorine, and a San Clemente afternoon will wreck a fresh tattoo. Wait until your artist says it is ready.
steps: Leave the bandage on for the time your artist told you. If they did not say, ask before you leave the chair.
Wash with mild unscented soap and lukewarm water. Pat dry. Do not scrub.
A thin layer of the ointment or lotion your artist recommended. Not a coat of grease.
No ocean, no pool, no hot tub, no soaking in the tub until healed.
No direct sun. No tanning. Cover it or stay in the shade. Fresh ink and Avenida sun do not mix.
No picking. No scratching. Let the skin do the work.
If it looks wrong — spreading redness, heat, pus, fever — call the shop and see a doctor.
aftercare.status: CONFIRM wording with Greg. This is general beach-town aftercare, not a medical protocol and not a substitute for what the artist tells you at the chair.

faq.q: How do I book an appointment?
faq.a: Call the shop or send a booking request. Appointments are held with a deposit. Amount and payment method: CONFIRM.

faq.q: How much does a tattoo cost?
faq.a: Depends on size, placement, cover-up work, and the artist. We do not publish a number here. Call or walk in and we will talk about the piece. CONFIRM if Greg wants a shop minimum listed.

faq.q: Can I get tattooed if I am under 18 with a parent?
faq.a: No. California has no parental exception for tattooing. You must be 18 and bring photo ID.
